A schema was committed as an empty file and every gate passed it #1103
Building a page finished before the things on it were built #1075
Card variants, footer links, collapsing panels and the behaviours workspace all render as their schemas describe

Every example image was broken on the published site. The site lives at two addresses. On your own machine it sits at the top level (localhost:3000/); published, it sits inside a folder (…github.io/wb-starter/). The examples asked for images starting from the top, /images/placeholder.svg, which finds the file on your machine but on the published site points outside the project entirely, to an address that does not exist. So every example image failed to load, and only ever for visitors. The page now adds the folder to those addresses before the examples render.

The first version of that fix missed every portfolio card. It re-rooted a fixed list of attribute names — src, image, avatar — and cover was not on it, so x-cardportfolio kept 404ing while the fix looked complete. A list of names is only as good as whoever last remembered to extend it, so the value now gets a vote: an attribute whose value ends in a media extension is an asset, whatever it is called.

Four checks were matching nothing at all. A \b word boundary written through a tool that eats escapes becomes a literal backspace character, which no real source contains — so the check silently passes forever. The guard that exists to catch exactly this scanned src, scripts and tests for code extensions only, and so could not see pages/behaviors.html: 2,500 lines of inline JavaScript, the largest body of source in the project. One of the dead checks was the warning that tells readers of the static site which examples need the local dev server — present, styled, and unable to fire. #1049

The version badge had no styling at all. release.css existed, was correct, and was loaded by nothing. When site.css stopped importing every behaviour stylesheet and switched to loading them on demand, each one had to be named in a manifest — and this one never was, so its three classes had no rules behind them on every page. A stylesheet that never loads raises no error and the element still renders its text, which is why nobody caught it. A new check fails if any behaviour stylesheet is reachable from nothing. #1008

Unshipped work was reported as delivered. The tool that says how far a fix has travelled counted a commit on any remote branch as “pushed”, so work sitting on a feature branch — where most work starts — read as shipped. Travel is now measured by reachability from the branch the site actually ships from; a commit that is only on a working branch stays “committed”, which is what it is. #1043

The deployed error viewer reported “No errors found. Great job!” while it was reading the wrong address. It fetched the log from the organisation root rather than from this site, got a 404, and treated that as “nothing has gone wrong” — a false all-clear on a site that had errors, which is worse than an error message. It now reads the log relative to itself, and when there genuinely is no log it says which address it checked, so a wrong path can never again look like good news. #1000

Sorting a date column sorted it by month name. Table sorting understood dates written the way data stores them (2026-09-03) but not the way pages print them (Sep 5, 2026), so a rendered date fell through to plain text sorting: April before March, January after February. On the issues list that put “Apr 1, 2025” ahead of “Mar 1, 2020” — five years out. Enough pairs came out right by accident that the column looked fine at a glance. Rendered dates are now compared as dates, and a column of ordinary text is still sorted as text. #1011

releases.summary: The queue could not report progress, so it looked like there was none. Four defects had compounded into one symptom: work that was finished, committed and pushed still showed as un-started. Three of them were in the tool that decides an issue’s state; the fourth was quietly deleting the evidence that tool reads. Also here: five interface fixes that had been waiting to land.

items.html: Nine out of ten commits were invisible to the issue tracker. The tool that works out how far a fix has travelled reads the git log, and it split that log on a separator the format only produces when a commit message has no body. Any commit with a description got glued to its neighbours and silently thrown away — 937 of 1,056. A well-written commit was the most likely to vanish, so a fix that had shipped left no trace and its issue reported as never started. #1042

An issue could not be marked pushed unless its test happened to run. Where a fix is — committed, pushed — is a fact about git, not about testing. But the check for “did its test run recently” sat above the check for “has this shipped”, and most runs are filtered to a handful of specs, so almost every issue fell back to unproven the moment it was committed. A failing test still outranks travel: shipping something does not make it work. #1042

Merely mentioning an issue counted as unfinished work on it. Any file containing #1234 was treated as a pending fix for that issue, which suppressed its real state. Release notes, handoff docs and standards all name issues in passing. The sharpest case: the state tool reported the wrong state for three issues because of its own comments explaining those three issues. #1041

Running the tests erased the record of the tests. Playwright empties its output directory at the start of every run, and that directory had been pointed at the same place the test reporter keeps its results — the results every gate and every status query reads. A filtered run wiped all five projects and wrote back almost nothing. Measured across two runs: issues ready 3 → 0, failing 7 → 0, unproven 5 → 18, with no work done to any of them. Playwright now has its own scratch directory. #1038

Issue state now keeps itself current. It was only ever recalculated when someone remembered to ask for it, which is why the board could sit stale for a day. A commit is the event that changes an issue’s state, so every commit now refreshes the issues it names. It runs after the commit is written and never blocks it.
Dialog samples had no way to close them. The native <dialog> examples rendered without a close control and with no padding, because the dialog behaviour never ran on them. #1005

The behaviours workspace had two vertical scrollbars. One container too many was scrolling, there was no gap at the side, and the footer stayed stuck in the document instead of anchored to the viewport. #1020
The language badge sat on top of the first line of every code sample. On the themes page it overlapped the code it was labelling. #1023
Sorting a table sorted the text you could see, not the value underneath. A column declaring a sort key was ignored, so dates and versions ordered alphabetically. Rows now move as whole rows. #1036

The demos index linked to a page that no longer exists. The Views Registry Browser was removed because it imports a module deleted with the component tags — the page could not run at all — but the link to it stayed behind. #980

releases.summary: The first patch on 4.0.0. Nine changes: three that stop the demo pages freezing, two that repair what the 4.0.0 rename broke, and four that fix pages rendering wrong — or, in one case, a gate that had not been running at all.

items.html: The cards page no longer freezes. demos/site/cards.html built all 293 demos before the page was interactive — measured at 13,680ms of total main-thread blocking, including one unbroken 9,110ms task. The page painted in 112ms and then locked up. It now builds what is on screen and the rest as you reach them: 952ms of blocking, longest task 346ms, 48 demos at load instead of 293. The same change is on eleven sibling demo pages.

Code renders coloured on the first frame. A code panel used to appear as plain text at 234ms and only get syntax highlighting at 741ms — half a second of unstyled monospace. The panel is now held back until it has been highlighted, so there is no uncoloured frame at all. Measured cost of the change: 1ms.

Code panels stopped creeping wider. The shrink-to-fit measurement wrote its answer on every one of up to 25 polls, so each intermediate width was painted and the box visibly stepped outward while you read it. The value is now committed once, when it stops moving.

The site went down, and came back. The first performance push carried one renamed identifier whose other half stayed behind: a module asked for an export that no longer existed under that name. An unresolved import is not a small error — the module never runs, nothing that depends on it runs, and the whole page stops at Loading…. Every route, everyone, until it was fixed. The HTML, the CSS and every asset were served perfectly the entire time, which is exactly why nothing noticed.

Two tests now stand where nothing stood. One reads every module and checks that each thing imported is genuinely exported by the file it names — it fails on the exact change that caused the outage. The other opens five real pages and fails if any of them logs an error or is still showing Loading…. Both were verified by deliberately reintroducing the fault and confirming they go red, not merely by watching them pass.

Deploying now has a rule. A push is not finished when the files land; it is finished when the published site has been opened and proven to boot. Checking that the right content was uploaded is not a substitute — during the outage that check passed.

Compliance collected zero tests for twelve days. A spec built a regex containing [x-demo] at module scope. That is a character class, so x-d reads as a range from x (120) to d (100) — endpoints reversed — and constructing it threw SyntaxError: Range out of order in character class at load. Playwright treats a collection-time throw as fatal for the whole project, so test:compliance reported “Total: 0 tests” and exited having checked nothing. The gate looked green because it never ran. CI had been red on every main run since 2026-08-21 for this reason, and every branch cut from main in that window was effectively ungated. (#975)

“Component” is gone from the vocabulary. 4.0.0 deleted every custom element; there is no Shadow DOM and no <wb-*> or <x-*> tag left, so the word described nothing that still exists — “Web Components” included. Reader-facing occurrences went 2,068 → 168 (92%), with 3,665 renames across 636 files.

Angular’s API name was renamed too, and the demo threw. That sweep reached executable code referencing a third-party API: @angular/core exports Component and has never exported Behavior, so the frameworks demo died on load with Behavior is not a function. Restored at all four sites in both copies. The template copy is the one that mattered — it ships, so every project scaffolded by create-wb-starter got a demo page that threw. (#971)

The behaviors reference hung the renderer. docs/behaviors-reference.md closed three <div> elements with </input>. input is a void element with no closing tag, so the parser discarded each one, leaving the divs open and the document nesting wrong from that point down.

The table behavior rendered an empty table. The showcase decodes HTML entities for display and re-injects the result — and decoded, the JSON quotes in rows="[["alert",…]]" collide with the attribute delimiter, so the value terminated at [[ and the behavior received nothing. (#861)

Progress bars ignored striped. Two implementations existed: the tag map resolved [x-progressbar] to one module, while anything deriving the name by stripping x- loaded a second one with different classes, inline styles, and a striped that only answered to striped="true". The showcase derives it that way, so a bare striped rendered plain there while working everywhere else. Search typing now filters, and a permutation check that never actually permuted was repaired.
API and Docs panels now fill the live panel and cover the example. Previously they opened at the right position but stopped short of the bottom, leaving the example visible underneath.

The site still said v3.0, and the home page had no <h1>. The title was declared in four places — three in index.html (<title>, og:title, twitter:title) and once in config/site.json — and site-engine.js overwrote document.title at runtime from the config, so fixing any one place did nothing.

releases.summary: Breaking. Every <wb-*> component tag is gone. Nothing in this repo writes components any more — you write real HTML and add behavior with an x- attribute.

items.html: 155 component tags removed. 104 lived in tag-map.js, 18 more in wb-lazy.js — a second registry that a search of the first would never have found — and 33 were unprefixed aliases (basic-card, hero-card, profile-card, card-image) that a search for wb- would have missed entirely.

No behavior was lost. Every tag had a replacement before it was deleted. 18 became the semantic element that already auto-injects them — <wb-card> is now <article>, <wb-dialog> is <dialog>, <wb-progress> is <progress>. The rest became a host element carrying the behavior as an attribute: <wb-alert> is <div x-alert>.

Eleven behaviors were reachable only through their tag — container, grid, center, cover, switcher, reel, frame, icon, stat, sidebarlayout and modal. Deleting those tags would have deleted the behaviors with them, so x-container, x-grid, x-center and the rest were added first.

The wb-views system is gone. <wb-view> was a component tag, and its 1,006-line implementation ran on every page load — fetching two registries and 47 partials — to serve a feature no page in pages/ ever used.

94 tags in the markup were never implemented at all. <wb-btn>, <wb-code>, <wb-menu-item>, <wb-breadcrumb-item> and 90 others appeared in pages, docs and the project template while being registered nowhere. They rendered as unknown inline elements and always had — teaching a vocabulary that did not exist, including to every new project scaffolded from the template.

docs/components/ is gone; there is one doc tree now. Of its 96 files, 65 duplicated a docs/behaviors/ page and 12 were index files for the tree itself. The 19 with unique content moved across, and the component docs that said more than their behavior counterpart were merged rather than dropped — x-card.md alone carried 3.3KB of guidance that card.md did not have.

Attribute names follow the semantic element, with no exceptions. All 26 native mappings were audited: <table>→table→x-table reads straight down, and now every row does. x-img is registered at last — docs/behaviors/img.md had been teaching it in four places while only x-image existed, so following the documentation produced no behavior and no error. x-radio, x-range and x-mark were missing entirely and have been added.

A new audit checks all six selector registries at once. Behaviors are bound in six places across three files, and reading one of them is how a behavior comes to look missing when it is not. npm run audit:behavior-registry reports every disagreement and fails on the ones that matter. It found the second element registry that this very migration had missed.

A glowing button responds when you press it. The continuous effects — glow, rainbow, particle — bind no click handler, so a button carrying one looked pressable, got pressed, and did not move. It now goes down on press and comes back on release, held long enough to be seen (a real click can start and finish inside one frame). Keyboard activation counts as a press too, and releasing off the element still lets it come back up.

Overlay cards left gaps either side. The card had an aspect ratio and no width, so it sized itself from its height and floated in the middle of its container. It fills the container now, with the height following from the ratio instead of the other way round.
The playground cannot be held by a browser. It is edited constantly, and a held copy is indistinguishable from a fix that did not work.

The playground was never cache-busted, so fixes to it looked like they never shipped. Only the two SPA shells were stamped, and the pattern matched src/… and ./src/… but not ../src/… — which is how every page under demos/ and pages/ reaches its CSS and modules. 18 files are stamped now, where it was 2.
The playground no longer hosts a component gallery. 289 lines and 53 examples in retired wb- tags, sitting under an editor meant for your own markup.

The x-behaviors example had no card behaviors at all — 19 of them, the largest family, absent from a set that claims to show the behaviors. They are pulled from the same data the showcase renders, so they cannot drift. The count in the label is generated now instead of written by hand.
A button labelled "Glow" invited a click and did nothing. It is a continuous effect, not a click-triggered one; the label now says so.

A false error on every native input. A warning added days ago told authors that <input input-type="text"> "cannot build a field" — but an <input> IS the field, and input-type maps to its type. It fired on correct markup and filled the error log. The warning now only fires where a host genuinely cannot build one, and input-type is applied.

Copy did not copy. The clipboard API is refused for reasons unrelated to the page, and the fallback said "Press Ctrl+C" — impossible advice, since nothing was selected. It now falls back to a real copy and only reports failure when both paths fail.

collapsible did nothing you could see. The behavior toggled two classes that existed in no stylesheet. The legend now looks clickable, collapsing hides the contents, and collapsed fields leave the tab order.

A layout rule for ordinary media. The standards covered floating layers and padding but never said an image has to fit the box it renders in, so nothing was being violated — there was no rule. Added as §15a, with the constraint that also prevents upscaling.
Three tests. Every element in a rendered example carries a unique id; no example logs an error while rendering; and the stage leaves no dead space after a tall example.

The dialog example had no way to open it. It put title and content on the <dialog> itself — but in this framework an element carrying those IS the trigger, so the dialog had no trigger and nothing could reopen it once closed. The example now shows the pattern the behavior documents: a <dialog> whose children are its content, and a button that calls .open() on it.

x-accordion did nothing with <details> children. It collected its panels by looking for an accordion-title attribute, which a <details> does not carry — so it found none, built nothing, and three unrelated disclosures rendered. It now recognises them and adds the one thing that makes a set of disclosures an accordion: opening one closes the others. Native keyboard, screen-reader and find-in-page behaviour is untouched.
The first behavior is selected on arrival. The panel used to open empty, so the page arrived showing a list and a blank space.

Two tests that should have existed already. One measures the stage after a tall example then a short one — the sequence that produced four separate reports of dead space and survived three fixes because nobody measured the box. The other proves an accordion is exclusive, which "does it open" would not have caught.

Dead space above a short example, for real this time. The stage grows so an open dropdown or a fullscreen dialog has room, and that growth is dropped when a different example is shown — except the reset sat on only one of the two render paths. Generated examples took the other one and inherited the previous example's height, so a two-line details sat centred in a box sized for a fullscreen dialog. Reset once now, before either path runs.

Semantic listed x- tokens instead of element names. The check for "does this example use its semantic tag" built a word boundary as '\b' inside a string — which is the backspace character, not a boundary — so it matched nothing and every row was relabelled to its x- token. Semantic now lists article, button, dialog, progress.

The Filter radios did nothing. The list logic was right, but the change listener was bound with querySelectorAll while the page was still being wired, so it captured an empty list and never attached. Clicking Semantic left the list on Both — a filter that does not filter. Delegated now, so timing cannot break it.

With autoInject on, <article x-ripple> gets both behaviors again. 3.0.81 stopped an element being built twice by two behaviors, but it stood autoInject down for any x- attribute — so asking for a card with a ripple gave only a ripple. A replacement is a member of the tag behavior's own family (card → cardportfolio, cardimage); anything else decorates and stacks.

Filter the list by authoring form. Semantic shows the 22 behaviors a tag carries on its own; x-attribute shows all 143 reached by attribute; Both shows everything. Each row renders its own form, so the two are actually different.
Every behavior with a semantic tag now demonstrates both forms. Was 6 of 22.
67 card examples were built twice. The guard against two behaviors claiming one element required the second to be registered already — under lazy loading it usually is not, so both ran.
Collapsing a details example left the blank space behind. The stage only ever grew.
Button labels state their configuration — variant: primary · icon: download · size: md — instead of naming an action they do not perform.
Clicking any example resyncs the list to its row, and the documentation panel can be dragged to the top.

A demo label no longer promises something the demo cannot do. The button example read "Download report" — it is a styling demo, it downloads nothing, and a reader who clicked it learned only that the example lied. It reads "Button example of a primary button" now, matching the rule the other examples already follow. A compliance test fails any example label starting with an action verb it cannot carry out, because the single edit is worthless without it — the next hand-written example would put it straight back (#758).

Issue links in the last two releases pointed at issues that did not exist. Five fixes were shipped citing numbers that were never filed — the next ones in sequence, used as though the issues had been created. That put dead links in this page and in the source comments. The issues are filed now (#753–#757) and all 37 references across 8 files corrected.

A select's options never rendered. options="main,develop,fix/706-dropdown" — the comma-separated form the examples use — was passed to JSON.parse, threw, and the error was swallowed, leaving an empty dropdown and nothing to explain it. Both spellings work now, and malformed JSON raises a real error instead of rendering nothing (#756).

The clear button dwarfed the select it belonged to. It was built as a full button component, so it took a button's padding, and no rule for it existed anywhere to constrain the size. It is now a plain compact control sized in em, so it tracks the select's own size, with an accessible name and a visible focus ring (#757).

No retired wb- tags left in the behavior demos. One example still rendered a wb- table, and its own row data taught wb- component names. It is plain <table> now, which auto-injects, and the data names behaviors instead.

Input variants and sizes were dead on every host. Three causes, found by a permutation suite rather than one at a time: the container host built a field and applied neither, the native host read only data-size and never the plain size, and size="md" / variant="default" were skipped on purpose — leaving the schema's own defaults with no trace, indistinguishable from being ignored (#754).

<div x-input> rendered nothing at all. The field builder was gated on the host being <x-input>, so the documented authoring form produced no label, no field and no variant. It now builds on any container host; a host that IS a form control keeps the wrap path, where the element already is the input (#754).

A behavior that cannot honour your attributes now says so. Asking for label, helper, error or input-type on a host that cannot build a field raises a real runtime error naming the ignored attributes, instead of rendering nothing and looking broken (#754).

The events panel reports the element id, and only the id. It printed tag#id.class, burying the one token worth reading — and because the listener sits on the stage, a click on the stage's own padding was logged as if the example had fired it. Events outside the example are no longer reported at all (#755).

Permutation suites for input, and every x-* checked for impropriety. Both read their value lists from the schema and the tag-to-behavior map, so new values are covered without touching the tests. The x-* test swept 29 doc files still teaching <figure x-figure>, <img x-image>, <pre x-pre> and the rest, and the generator that would have put them all back (#753).

package.json and package-lock.json were empty on main for four releases. A version-bump script opened each file for writing before reading it — which truncates — so it wrote an empty string back. 3.0.71 through 3.0.75 shipped with both files blank, breaking every npm command against the repo. Restored from the last good copy and re-versioned; both parse.

A test that finds every x-* attribute and rejects the improper ones. <figure x-figure> is redundant — a <figure> auto-injects the behavior from its tag — and #746 showed the redundant form can silently suppress the behavior entirely. The test sweeps authored pages, demos, docs and the seeded example data, and drives the showcase to check every generated example, which is the path that produced <figure x-figure> in the first place. Tag-to-behavior pairs are read from the map itself, so new mappings are covered without touching the test (#753).

Generated examples stopped writing <figure x-figure>. 3.0.70 removed the redundant attributes from the seeded examples, but examples the showcase generates took a different decision: they asked whether a display label existed, and several behaviors have none — so <figure> fell through and got the attribute anyway. Whether a tag auto-injects a behavior is a fact about the tag-to-behavior map, not about whether someone wrote a label, so the generator now asks the map (#753).

<fieldset collapsible> did not collapse. The behavior read only data-collapsible, so the documented spelling was ignored and the demo rendered a plain fieldset — nothing told the reader the attribute was being dropped rather than broken. Plain attributes are now read alongside data-*, and collapsible="false" counts as OFF (#752).

The same defect is in 32 more places. Auditing it turned up 69 attribute reads across 32 behavior files that only check data-* while every schema, doc and example teaches the plain form. Three separate reports this week were the same bug fixed one site at a time. Catalogued with the full file list and a proposed shared reader plus per-behavior tests, so the class gets closed instead of the next instance (#752).

The dev-server notice was not appearing. 3.0.72 added it on one of the two paths that render an example, and the form demo happens to take the other, so the notice never showed on the very example it was written for — caught by checking the deployed page rather than the diff. Both paths now call it.

Examples that need the dev server say so on this site. The form demo posts to /api/…, a route a static host cannot serve — so on the published site it fails, and nothing told the reader the example is fine and the host is the limitation. Any example posting to /api/… now carries a notice, shown only off localhost, explaining that it needs the local dev server and linking the repo to clone and npm start (#751).

The form behavior never turned AJAX on. <form validate ajax> — the documented spelling — did nothing, because the behavior read only data-ajax. Submitting fell through to a plain form post, which is why nothing appeared to happen. Plain attributes are now read alongside their data-* equivalents for ajax, validate, auto-save and the three message strings, closing the same gap #697 closed for fieldset and formrow. ajax="false" is also honoured as OFF: a bare presence check reads the string "false" as ON, the opposite of what the markup says (#751, #747).

The form demo has a destination that answers. The example declared no action, so it posted to the page itself and the already-implemented success path was unreachable. It now targets a demo endpoint that accepts and discards, so the success message and the wb:form:success event actually fire. It deliberately sends no mail — a public endpoint that emails a user-supplied recipient is an open relay (#751).

Examples no longer write an attribute autoInject makes unnecessary. <fieldset x-fieldset> and <figure x-figure> taught a duplication the framework exists to remove — a semantic host gets its behavior from the tag alone. 13 redundant attributes removed across the examples. An x- naming a different behavior stays, because <button x-dialog> is the point of that example, not duplication. A compliance test now reads the tag-to-behavior map from its own source and fails the build if a redundant attribute reappears — the same class of defect that let x-button silently suppress the button behavior for three releases (#749, #746).

The button behavior was bailing on its own attribute. 3.0.67 fixed one of two gates; this fixes the one that actually mattered. The behavior treated any x- attribute as proof that a different behavior owned the element — including x-button itself — so it returned without adding a single class. Variants, sizes, icons and href are now live in both authoring forms (#746).

A permutation test suite for every button parameter. 26 tests reading their value lists from button.schema.json at runtime, so a value added to the schema is covered automatically: all 8 variants, all 5 sizes, all 40 variant×size pairs, all 20 icons, both icon positions, four booleans, disabled actually blocking activation, href with both targets, and an equivalence test asserting the bare and x-button forms produce identical classes. It caught the first fix being wrong before it could be called done (#746).
Example labels name the variant too. "Button example of a centered x-dialog" rather than just the behavior — the variant is what distinguishes one row of the list from the next (#746).

Every button example says which behavior it demonstrates. A button hosting x-dialog read "Delete branch…", a button hosting x-ripple read "With Ripple" — sample copy that told you nothing about what you were looking at. All 40 button-hosted examples now read "Button example of x-dialog", "Button example of x-ripple", and so on, matching the behavior named in the source beside them (#746).

Writing x-button turned the button behavior OFF. Variants, icons and sizes were all dead on any button carrying the attribute the docs teach. Measured side by side: <button x-button variant="outline" icon="download" size="md"> came out with class="" and no icon, while the identical button without x-button came out x-button x-button--md x-button--outline with its icon rendered. The native auto-inject path bailed whenever x-{behavior} was present, assuming the explicit attribute path would handle it — it does not, because the core never reads the map that x-button lives in, so the element fell between the two and got nothing. A same-named attribute no longer disqualifies the element; a genuinely different one still does (#746).

Fullscreen no longer centres the example in a screen of empty space. #711 gave the stage align-content: center so a short example would not pile its slack underneath itself in a panel-height box. At full screen that rule centred a single element in a 100vh box with screens of nothing above and below. Fullscreen has the opposite problem to the panel — there is more than enough room — so content now starts at the top and the example takes the width it is given (#746).

The documentation panel names its behavior. It read a bare "Documentation" under an example that changes with the selection, giving nothing to tie it to. It now reads "Button Documentation", "Details Documentation", and so on (#746).

The attribute table's Values column wraps at the viewport edge. An enum with 17 values ran off the right of the screen as one unbroken line, putting the last values out of reach. The column now wraps to the next row, and each value stays intact on its own line-box rather than being split down the middle (#746).
Details examples say what they are. The rendered summary read "Trail conditions" with nothing identifying it as a sample; it now reads "Details sample of Trail conditions" (#746).

Fullscreen now shows the navigator and the search, not just the rendered example. The button targeted #behaviors-live-example — the innermost wrapper around the rendered element — so going fullscreen left one example alone on a black screen with no way to reach another. #720 added fullscreen on the stage and #722 narrowed it to the example to kill the empty space around it; that removed the empty space and the navigation with it. The target is now the workspace: the search box and its count, the behaviors navigator, and the rendered side, all filling the screen with each column scrolling on its own, so a 170-entry list and a tall example stay usable at the same time. Exiting restores the previous layout unchanged (#744).

Reference links were legible in name only. 3.0.64 made them a different colour from the prose, but on the dark themes that colour measured rgb(51,51,204) — a dark indigo on a near-black panel, distinct but hard to read. The link colour now blends the theme's accent toward the theme's own text colour, so it keeps the accent hue and stays legible against whatever background a theme paints. One rule for all eight themes, rather than a per-theme override list that goes stale the next time a theme is added.

The cache-bust token was always one commit behind the change it existed to bust. stamp-version.js read git rev-parse --short HEAD, which during a pre-commit run is the parent commit — the commit being made does not exist yet. So a release that changed only CSS shipped with an unchanged ?v= and never reached any browser holding the old file. Measured: 3.0.63 deployed with ?v=80d6768, which is the 3.0.62 commit. The token is now the release version (?v=3.0.64): known before the commit, changed exactly when a release ships, and named the same as the release it belongs to.

New Error Log button at the bottom of the main menu, linking straight to the error viewer.

Real runtime errors were only ever showing up in your browser's own devtools console — the site's own error log and error viewer never actually received them. Fixed the wiring; errors now land in both places.
The notes drawer now automatically files a real GitHub issue for every note you save, instead of just sitting in a local file nobody reviews.

On the Behaviors page (and everywhere else), examples decorated with an x-* attribute (like x-toast, x-ripple) now get the same clickable "docs" icon in the corner that components already had, instead of a plain text link easy to miss.
Every size and color variant of the dropdown/select control now actually looks different — they used to render almost identically regardless of which size or variant you picked.
Changing the theme in one place (like the header) now instantly updates every other theme picker on the page — they used to fall out of sync until you reloaded.
Fixed a drawer/sidebar toggle button that threw an error on every click after the first.
Fixed a navigation bar crash that could happen when it contained custom link markup.
x-audio's documentation examples pointed at audio files that never existed — replaced with real, working audio.
Demos page: each category is now one clickable card (title + description together), instead of a description sitting above a separate, smaller "view" link.
Added documentation for 9 previously-undocumented layout behaviors (center, masonry, sticky, scrollable, sidebarlayout, switcher, cover, reel, icon).
Demo blocks can now show you how to listen for the events a control fires — add it to a demo and see a live log update as you interact with the control above it.

Fixed several component bugs: card glass+elevated variants losing their glass look, video cards with no fixed aspect ratio, a heading-margin rule losing to a more specific unrelated rule on the Components page, and a stale page generator that would have undone several of these fixes if it had been re-run.
<input type="password"> now gets the show/hide toggle automatically, just like type="checkbox"/type="radio"/type="range" already did — no more redundant x-password attribute needed.
Fixed a real double-border on styled inputs (Success/Error variants showed two concentric rings) — a wrapper div was reusing the same CSS class as the input it wrapped.
Fixed the Components page's section headings sitting too close to their content — a page-specific spacing rule was silently losing to a more specific rule elsewhere and never actually applying.

Notes drawer, rebuilt: notes now save to a real file (not just this browser's local storage), support pasting a screenshot directly into a note, can capture a reference to any element on the page you click, and got a cleaner layout (Save/New at the bottom, Close pinned to the corner, a searchable Lookup for past notes).
Fixed the Content page's searchable table — the search box never actually appeared.
Product cards with a broken image now retry and show a clear failed state instead of a silent empty box forever, matching image/video cards.
45+ components no longer carry a redundant CSS class that just repeats their own tag name (this rule is now enforced project-wide, not just for the components caught so far).
The "Forced Dark/Light/Cyberpunk Mode" theme demos now render as real, properly-styled cards instead of a plain unstyled box.
Stats cards' Compact/Large variants, and Product cards' Horizontal variant, now actually look different from the default — previously the variant class was added but no CSS ever consumed it.
Expandable cards gained a lines option to clamp collapsed text to an exact number of lines, instead of an arbitrary pixel height that could cut off mid-word.

Fixed the Copy button demo silently copying the wrong text (it read an attribute name the component doesn't actually use), and the Dark Mode Toggle demo doing nothing at all when clicked — both now also look like real buttons instead of bare text.
The footer now auto-hides on scroll in mobile landscape mode, same as the header already did, to reclaim screen space.
<x-demo> blocks with no explicit column count now default to a single column instead of three.
Card Components demo: several images/avatars didn't match their card's stated topic or person, and some links went nowhere real — fixed across the gallery.
Documentation: split V3-GUIDE §3 from a cramped 6-component <x-demo> into 6 separate ones per standard #2/#17/#18 — improved readability and component isolation (#483).
Performance: widened wb-lazy.js lazy-injection rootMargin from 200px to 1200px — components now begin loading sooner and feel more responsive on scroll (#491).
Fixed docs/manifest.json 404ing on the root SPA (/index.html) — every component's "Docs:" link on the main site was silently dead.
45 components (<x-card>, <x-button>, <x-badge>, and more) no longer carry a redundant CSS class that just repeated their own tag name.

Fixed WB.scan() never processing the exact element passed to it (only its descendants) — this was silently breaking syntax highlighting, line numbers, and the copy button on every dynamically-injected code panel site-wide.

Framework Integration Demo: removed a legacy, duplicate code-highlighting system that was clipping the left edge of every code sample; Svelte and SolidJS examples now compile and render live in the browser (Angular can't without a real build step — explained why, on the page).
Playground: the 20-video YouTube example now grids 3-per-row instead of one huge column; sample form labels now sit above their field instead of beside it.
The site's browser-tab title and social-share preview card showed generic placeholder text ("My Awesome Site") instead of real branding — fixed, with proper preview images added.
Fixed flat, non-responsive page padding eating up to 38% of small phone screens across 11 pages — a full-width hero image was reading as a narrow strip because of it.
Every clickable button, card, and switch across the demo pages now shows a quick confirmation toast when clicked.
Card Components demo: added a theme picker, and replaced placeholder links/identity (generic example.com URLs, a stock "Jane Doe") with real destinations.
Fixed the profile card's role badge sitting visibly off-center on its cover photo (a repeat of an earlier "fix" that didn't actually center it).
Fixed the theme picker silently duplicating itself into two out-of-sync dropdowns over a long browsing session.
Removed several redundant x-fieldset/x-form attributes that were already automatic — added a test that catches this pattern going forward.

Fixed <x-input> rendering no real <input> element at all on any standalone demo page (32 broken instances on the Form Controls page alone) — the schema-driven markup it depends on was never built under this site's lazy-loading runtime. It's now constructed directly, matching how other components already handle this.
Fixed the theme picker breaking syntax-highlighting colors site-wide on any page that includes it — it was resolving to a dev-only file path that doesn't exist in production.
Fixed silent failures across the site being swallowed instead of shown — component errors now surface in the visible error log instead of vanishing into the console.
<x-button icon="..."> now throws a clear error (with a link to the icon list) if set but left empty, instead of silently rendering no icon.
Fixed <x-audio> silently doing nothing on a missing/empty file — it now throws a clear error, and 8 broken audio examples on the Content page were pointed at a real audio file.
Fixed the Shop Now / Learn More buttons on the Card Components hero demo, and the pricing/portfolio CTA buttons on Card Components and the main Components page — all had no destination before today.
Fixed the theme picker showing up twice (unsynced) on some pages — consolidated to one, in the site header.

Fixed the doc-link icon disappearing on the home page hero card, a role badge sitting too low on profile cards, the avatar status dot being too small, a dropdown menu getting clipped when it opened upward, an input field showing three stacked borders instead of one, and the date/time picker icon being invisible in dark mode.
Fixed <x-select> silently discarding real <option> children — every documented example (<x-select><option>...</option></x-select>) rendered an empty dropdown with only the placeholder.

Fixed <x-draggable>/x-draggable jumping to a wildly wrong position on every drag instead of tracking the mouse — and getting worse with each subsequent drag. Also fixed axis="x"/axis="y", which never actually constrained movement.

The Behaviors page no longer mixes in 15 full wb-* component demos (alerts, badges, progress bars, spinners, modals, drawers, tabs, accordion, audio player, switch, rating) — it's scoped back to genuine x-* attribute behaviors, with links to the Components page for the rest.

Fixed the deprecated <x-checkbox>/<x-textarea> wrapper elements on the Form Controls demo page — converted to native <input type="checkbox">/<textarea>, which already get the same styling with no wrapper needed.
The home page no longer eagerly fetches the entire page-builder partial library (20+ files) on load — those now load lazily, only when a page actually uses one.

<x-demo>'s code sample panel now scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping, and spans full width on mobile (≤700px) so scrolling past a page of demos doesn't jitter the page width — desktop still hugs each demo's own content.
Added a size attribute to x-gallery for fixed-size thumbnails (e.g. size="150px"), independent of the columns count.

Fixed a sanitizer bug in the markdown renderer that silently ate any attribute whose name contained "on" followed by more letters before its own = (e.g. options='...') — this was corrupting JSON-in-attribute examples site-wide, including live <x-select> dropdowns that quietly lost all their options.
Fixed <x-cardportfolio>'s variant, size, and availability-status indicator — none of them had any visible effect before today.
Fixed <x-timeline> not rendering at all (missing a base display: block).

Fixed <x-drawer> on standalone demo pages: it showed generic placeholder text instead of its real content, "top"/"bottom" positions rendered identically to "left", and the variant attribute (default/overlay/push) had no effect at all.

Fixed <x-dropdown>: position values didn't match the real attribute names so every position looked the same, menus opened empty when using plain text content, and trigger="hover" never actually worked.
Fixed progress bars and other enum-variant showcase pages rendering at 0%/invisible because the demo generator never filled in a representative value.
Added a real button-like appearance (background, border, cursor) to dialog/drawer/dropdown triggers that previously looked like plain unstyled text.
Fixed inline code chips and code blocks wrapping mid-word instead of scrolling or breaking at real word boundaries, on the Components page and the frameworks demo.
Every demo's "read the docs" link now sits as a small badge in the component's own top-right corner instead of a detached line below the whole group.
Converted every remaining static code example on the Select doc page and the full Behavior Cross-Reference doc (159 examples) into live, rendered demos.
Fixed 8 standalone demo pages that had zero padding, so headings and text sat flush against the browser edge.

Closed out a large batch of compliance-gate debt: reduced excess !important CSS usage back under the project's own limit, fixed a broken page-fragment generator that was shipping full HTML documents where the app expected bare fragments, fixed 10 pages' stylesheet links that 404'd under this site's actual deployed URL, and cleared out stale px-to-rem and data-attribute audit failures.

Fixed a Playwright-suite-wide "app ready" race: dozens of tests waited on the WB object existing, which is true before the app actually finishes initializing — now they wait for the real ready signal.
Restored the Behaviors page's missing content (spinner, and more) by regenerating it from its own schema, and fixed two stale button/alert markup patterns flagged by the compliance gate.
Rewrote a large batch of stale, pre-broken tests (dead entry points, renamed files, old CSS class names) so they test what the code actually does today.
Added margins/padding to the Card Components demo page and restored a missing closing </html> tag.
Added this "What's New" page.
Split the Card Components demo page apart from its 56-card permutation test matrix — the demo page loads faster and the matrix now has its own dedicated test fixture.
Deprecated <x-checkbox>/<x-textarea> in favor of native <input type="checkbox">/<textarea> with attributes — no more reinventing what the browser already does.
Fixed the Playground's "Endpoint sees" panel showing unconditionally instead of respecting its hidden state.
Fixed a 404 in the code-highlighting fallback loader.
Fixed <x-search> never getting its variant/size CSS classes.
Fixed cardhero variants, cardproduct badges, a lazy-demo scanning bug, an error-log race condition, and button-transition test flakiness.
Fixed lightbox, alert variants, countdown, YouTube embeds, and a cardimage race condition that made valid images falsely show "unavailable."
Consolidated demo pages into 8 clear categories, up from a sprawling flat index.
Fixed dispatch collisions where multiple behaviors fought over the same host element (switch, checkbox, select, textarea, input, button).
Added just-in-time CSS loading for behaviors — no more shipping every behavior's stylesheet on every page.
Fixed a CLS (layout shift) regression in the grid layout.
Added a selectable debug-trace category filter for easier troubleshooting.
